summary: Verified the Spoof-Tunnel CLI toolkit (C core + bash installer + whiptail manager). Focus: install.sh resilience against a broken third-party apt repo (ookla/speedtest-cli), bash syntax health of both scripts, and prebuilt binary ELF architecture + --help output. This is a CLI/network tool, not a web app — no HTTP endpoints or frontend to test.

tests_executed.details: Class=ELF64, Type=EXEC, Machine=Advanced Micro Devices X86-64.

tests_executed.name: /app/bin/spooftun-arm64 --help
tests_executed.details: Container runs on aarch64. Binary prints full usage block (subcommands run/probe-send/probe-listen + all options) and exits with code 0.

tests_executed.name: install.sh dep-block with broken ookla apt repo planted (happy path, tools already installable)
tests_executed.details: Planted /etc/apt/sources.list.d/zz-broken-test.list containing 'deb https://packagecloud.io/ookla/speedtest-cli/ubuntu noble main'. Ran the exact dep-installation block (lines 42-73 of install.sh) via /app/tests/test_install_deps.sh. Observed: (a) 'NOTE: apt-get update reported errors (a broken third-party repo?).' printed; (b) the specific 'does not have a Release file' line was grep'd and re-echoed with '! ' prefix; (c) 'Continuing with the working Ubuntu repositories...' printed; (d) script did NOT abort at apt-get update; (e) subsequent apt-get install succeeded from cached Debian repos and MISSING array was empty -> exit 0. Broken-repo file cleaned up afterwards.

tests_executed.name: install.sh dep-block ERROR path (simulated: tools missing after install attempt)
tests_executed.details: Ran /app/tests/test_install_deps_missing.sh which forces MISSING to contain all required tools. Verified: ERROR message 'required tools failed to install: git whiptail wg iptables ip' printed, followed by the exact remediation block including 'sudo rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*speedtest* /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*ookla*' and the re-run curl command, and the script exits with code 1 as required.

tests_executed.name: Cleanup of test apt sources
tests_executed.details: Confirmed /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ no longer contains any zz-broken-test*.list after tests. Only pre-existing debian.sources, mongodb-org-7.0.list, nodesource.list remain.

critical_code_review_comments: install.sh: apt-get update is correctly wrapped with 2>/tmp/spooftun_apt.log and treated as non-fatal via 'if ! ... ; then'. Under 'set -euo pipefail' this is the correct idiom (the failing command inside the if condition does NOT trigger errexit). Verified behavior matches spec.

install.sh line 55: 'apt-get install ... || true' silently swallows install errors — this is fine here because the MISSING check on lines 58-73 catches the real failure and produces an actionable message. Good design.

install.sh line 67: the wildcard rm pattern 'sudo rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*speedtest* /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*ookla*' covers both packagecloud (ookla) and any speedtest-named files — good coverage.
spoof-tunnel.sh (management CLI): only syntax-checked as requested. Not exercised because whiptail interactive menus cannot be driven from this non-TTY container.

Container limitation (expected, NOT a bug): CAP_NET_RAW is not granted in this Kubernetes pod, so raw-socket, IP spoofing, and WireGuard tunnel establishment cannot be exercised. Only --help was executed on the core binary.
seed_data_creation: Temporarily created /etc/apt/sources.list.d/zz-broken-test.list and zz-broken-test2.list to simulate the broken ookla repo. Both files were removed after tests completed; only pre-existing sources remain in /etc/apt/sources.list.d/.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Project is a pure CLI/network tool — no web backend or frontend to test. Do not use curl/playwright. Container is aarch64, so /app/bin/spooftun-arm64 runs natively but /app/bin/spooftun-amd64 needs qemu (not installed). Raw sockets / WireGuard cannot run here (missing CAP_NET_RAW) — this is expected. Reusable regression scripts live in /app/tests/test_install_deps*.sh; always clean up /etc/apt/sources.list.d/zz-broken-test*.list after running them.
rca of the issue: Original bug: 'curl ... install.sh | sudo bash' aborted on user's Ubuntu server because a stale ookla/speedtest-cli packagecloud apt source returned 404 for its Release file, and 'apt-get update' returned non-zero under 'set -e'. Fix (already applied in /app/install.sh lines 46-73): (1) apt-get update's stderr is captured to /tmp/spooftun_apt.log and its non-zero exit is caught in an 'if' guard (which is not affected by errexit), a NOTE + the offending Release-file line are printed, and execution continues; (2) apt-get install is best-effort (|| true); (3) real success is verified by probing for each required binary (git, whiptail, wg, iptables, ip) and, only if any is missing, printing a clear ERROR with the exact remediation command to remove the ookla source before exiting 1. Verified via /app/tests/test_install_deps.sh (happy path) and /app/tests/test_install_deps_missing.sh (ERROR path).
